Aquarium staff know the
octopus as an escape artist.
There are many accounts
of octopuses leaving their
tanks at night,
crossing wet floors to
reach other tanks,
and returning home before
morning.
The most famous case is Inky.
Inky lived at the
National Aquarium of New
Zealand in 2016.
Staff believe Inky slipped
through a small gap
at the top of
his tank, crossed about
eight feet of floor,
and squeezed into a
drainpipe roughly fifty
meters long that led
to the sea.
Octopuses also seem to
learn from cause and effect.
At the Sea Star
Aquarium in Coburg,
Germany, an octopus named
Otto reportedly squirted
a jet of water
at a bright lamp
above his tank,
apparently to switch it off.
The short circuit cut
the power to the
whole aquarium, and the
lamps were later hung higher.
In laboratory studies,
octopuses have solved a
number of puzzles.
An octopus given a
crab inside a clear
jar with a screw
lid has been reported
to learn how to
unscrew the lid.
These stories point to
problem solving, although
many are individual
observations rather than
large controlled studies.
Octopuses can even tell
individual humans apart.
At the Seattle Aquarium,
researchers worked with
eight giant Pacific
octopuses and two people
in the same T-shirt.
One person always fed
them, and the other
touched them with a
bristly stick.
After two weeks,
the octopuses behaved
differently toward the two.
The study was small,
and it is not
clear which cues they used.
In a study published
in 2009, researchers in
Indonesia described veined
octopuses carrying coconut
shell halves across the
sea floor in an
awkward, stilt-walking way.
When a threat appeared,
they assembled the two
halves into a shelter.
The researchers considered
this the first documented
case of tool use
in an invertebrate.
Another sign of a
curious mind may be play.
Researchers reported that
captive octopuses blew
floating plastic pill
bottles toward a stream
of water, let them
drift back, and blew
them out again,
over and over.
Scientists described this
as play-like behavior.
Proving play in animals
is difficult.
From escapes to pranks
to tools, the octopus
keeps surprising us.
For the full story
of this alien mind,
watch the full video
on Miya's Lab,
and subscribe for the
next one.
